newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's banks should have a better year.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's banks should have a better year.

text.p: After seriously underperforming the stock market last year, Portugal's banks look a much better bet in 1997, analysts say.
Improving interest margins, the disappearance of fears over capital calls and the country's improving economic outlook will combine to increase the attraction of the overall sector.

"We are betting on a better year for banks," said analyst Pedro Assuncao of brokers Central Investimentos. The analyst said that he expected the sector to perform at least as well as the overall index this year.
Last year, for example, Banco Comercial Portugues, the country's largest non-state bank, gained only six percent against a 35 percent surge in the PSI20 index of leading stocks.

Banco Comercial was particularly weighed down by investor uncertainties over the restructuring that followed its takeover of Banco Atlantico Portugues, but other Portuguese banks did not fare much better.

Banco Espirito Santo, one of the better performers after announcing that it was not interested in takeovers and therefore not a candidate for a significant capital call, still lagged the overall market with a gain of some 21 percent.
But while the outlook for the sector as a whole was improving, some bank shares were likely to do better than others, with BCP probably the best-placed of all, analysts said.
"We prefer BCP...looking at the fundamentals we like it more than the others," said Assuncao.
Analysts said that BCP would be able to make significant cost savings in 1997 after announcing job cuts of 1,000 -- around 15 percent of personnel -- at the end of 1996.

Banco Totta & Acores, while it was probably a good short-term play because of an anticipated high dividend yield on its 1996 results, was still plagued by uncertainties over the group's strategy, they said.
The bank is seen paying out 180-190 escudos per share for last year which at the current share price would give a yield of near six percent.
But the Champalimaud group, which also controls Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor and Banco Chemical Portugal, has yet to give a clear picture of how their activities will be coordinated.
Analysts said that investors were expecting that the banking interests would need to be restructured before the end of 1998.
Banco Portugues de Investimento is another bank that needs to spell out clearly to investors its plans for the group after taking over Banco de Fomento & Exterior last year, they said.
